title: High Ground
description: High ground entries into reverse half nelson, d'arce, seated kata gatame, reverse donkey, ankle lock, and triangle options.

skills.name: High Ground to Reverse Half Nelson

media.title: High Ground: New No-Gi Attack System Explained | B-Team Technique
notes: Context: this chapter starts from seated high ground, then uses the opponent's elbow reactions to climb into reverse half nelson.
- [00:32-00:57] He defines high ground as a chest wrap high on the chest and starts from seated high ground.
- [03:23-04:12] When the elbows come in, he shifts from crucifix pressure into reverse half nelson and starts looking for side triangle / armbar routes.
- [06:51-07:18] The top-arm trap helps bait d'arce entries while keeping inside elbow position.

media.title: Options from High Ground (Full Instructional) - V.O.W. BJJ
notes: Context: this section gives the broader high-ground entry mechanics for getting into reverse half nelson and related high-ground follow-ups.
- [01:20-03:36] He emphasizes wrapping high on the chest, pinching the elbows, and stepping high past the opponent's knee so the fall is not just a strength-based pull.
- [03:39-05:30] Once he falls to the side, he treats the position as interchangeable left or right as long as he commits and windshield-wipers his legs out when needed.
- [05:32-06:59] From the side, he explains that the opponent's reaction can lead into reverse half nelson, turtle, two-on-ones, or crucifix entries while preserving the same high-ground control.

skills.name: Reverse Half Nelson to Seated Kata Gatame

media.title: High Ground: New No-Gi Attack System Explained | B-Team Technique
notes: Context: this segment starts from high ground, then uses the reverse half nelson branch to expose a seated head-and-arm finishing lane.
- [09:28-09:56] He hooks the outside leg, switches toward front head, and pulls the arm through to trap the shoulder line.
- [10:27-10:55] From the same setup he keeps the arm isolated and moves through nearby triangle and armbar options if the head-and-arm finish does not settle.

media.title: High Ground: New No-Gi Attack System Explained | B-Team Technique
notes: Context: this video shows the high-ground / reverse half nelson branch that keeps the top-arm trap available for d'arce attacks.
- [05:05-06:14] From high ground, he blocks the elbow, collects reverse half nelson, and follows the turn-in reaction into the d'arce finish.
- [06:20-06:51] He also shows a roll-through entry that reconnects elbow to knee and comes up into the same d'arce-catching game.
- [10:51-11:45] He explains that trapping the top arm makes it easier to shoot the elbow through and bait the d'arce.

media.title: Options from High Ground (Full Instructional) - V.O.W. BJJ
notes: Context: this section builds a reaction-based d'arce game from high ground and reverse half nelson: the opponent's turn determines which side you attack, and staying tight opens nearby neck-tie/anaconda options.

- [12:35-13:33] From high ground and reverse half nelson, when the opponent rotates toward him, he redirects the top arm across, releases the bottom arm, spins with the rotation, and catches a tight d'arce.

- [14:07-15:04] He shows the d'arce on the opposite side too: if the opponent will not turn toward him, he releases the arm, lets the opponent rotate away, moves north-south, and catches the bottom-arm side.
- [15:14-17:09] If the opponent refuses to rotate either direction, he switches to the nearby neck-tie/anaconda family instead of forcing the d'arce.
- [19:43-20:06] If he comes up and the opponent is too strong to finish immediately, he can release, return to the d'arce threat, and resend the same pressure cycle.

media.title: Options from High Ground (Full Instructional) - V.O.W. BJJ
notes: Context: this is the leg-pummeling branch he reaches when the high-ground exchange leaves him controlling the hips but needing to retract his knees and thread his legs back into the position.
- [30:30-31:04] He warns that simply holding the hips is not enough; he has to retract his legs and start pummeling them back into useful controls.
- [31:52-32:28] He bridges onto his shoulder, threads a leg across, and scoops into the X-shaped leg configuration.
- [32:28-33:15] He describes this as reverse donkey guard, locks the position in, and starts attacking the foot / big toe.

media.title: Options from High Ground (Full Instructional) - V.O.W. BJJ
notes: Context: once reverse donkey guard is set, he covers two finishes from the ankle-lock grip: the Aoki lock and the Woj lock.
- [33:31-33:43] He scoops over the top of the knee, gets the ankle-lock grip, posts, and finishes with the Aoki lock.
- [33:43-34:07] If the first foot position changes, he follows into the Woj lock variation and keeps rotating through the finish.
- [34:07-34:30] If the foot kicks free, he recaptures the leg and keeps the same rotation going.
- [34:30-34:44] If the legs get away entirely, he comes up, recaptures, and pulls the opponent back into the leg position.

media.title: Options from High Ground (Full Instructional) - V.O.W. BJJ
notes: Context: he frames these triangle options as a follow-up to the reverse-donkey leg attacks: the leg attacks make the opponent rotate, and that rotation lets him feed his legs into triangles.
- [31:08-31:23] He says he often uses the triangles to sweep, get on top, or change the position, even though they can become finishes.
- [34:44-35:23] If the opponent rotates the wrong way, he gets up on his shoulder and feeds his legs into tight triangle finishes.
- [35:43-35:53] The goal is to bait the turn one way or the other and finish the triangle tightly.
